title: Summit and Compass
premise: Hazel Halloran, a desert ranger who survives by never staying anywhere long enough to be remembered, is hired to track a thief across the salt flats. Instead of the thief, the dry riverbed yields a chest bearing the seal of Vessia, a nation erased from every map forty years ago — and Hazel realizes they are the last living person who ever called it home. The chest holds an expedition ledger pointing to a glacier cache that opens only during calving season, a two-week window when the ice route is passable. Hazel must assemble and lead a crew to retrieve what's inside without revealing their own buried identity, then choose between selling the find, destroying it, or finally claiming a name they've spent a lifetime outrunning.
about_author: Mirabel Blackwood is the pen name of a former field cartographer who spent six years mapping ephemeral waterways in arid basins. They write adventure fiction about people whose survival depends on being forgotten.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hired by a nervous magistrate to track a thief who stole nothing but a map fragment, Hazel crosses the salt flats and finds the thief dead at a dry riverbed, clutching a sealed chest stamped with Vessia's crest. The emotional beat is dread: Hazel recognizes the seal instantly, and with it, the first crack in the identity they've built. They take the chest because leaving it means someone else will open it.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, intercut with ledger entries from the lost Vessian expedition. Inside the chest: a route log to a glacier cache, a photograph of a family Hazel doesn't remember but whose faces feel like home, and a list of names — one of which is Hazel's birth name. The beat is vertigo; memory returns in fragments as Hazel realizes the thief was hunting their past, not their money.

chapters.title: Calving Season
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs as Hazel recruits three strangers for the ice crossing under a false expedition charter, racing the calving window while a Vessian descendant society — alerted by the missing chest — closes in. On the glacier, the cache is found, but so is evidence someone reached it decades ago and chose to leave it sealed. The climax: Hazel must decide, on cracking ice, whether the truth is worth more than survival.

chapters.title: A Name Returned
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The crew comes home through the closing pass carrying only the ledger, having burned the rest — except Hazel keeps the photograph. They deliver a sanitized report, collect their pay, and for the first time stay in one town past the point where staying becomes dangerous. The resolution: identity isn't something you escape or reclaim, but something you choose daily. Hazel signs a new register with an old name, freely given.
